steps.say: When the two ends of the food pipe lie too far apart for immediate joining, the baby lives for months with saliva draining out and milk going straight into the stomach. A suction tube keeps the upper pouch empty, nursing stays upright and tilted, and feeds pass through a tube in the abdominal wall.
steps.tx: **Pure atresia** (gap too wide) needs a **gastrostomy** (stomach feeding tube) since primary joining is impossible neonatally. Secretions are managed by indwelling tube **suction** (sump drainage), **prone upright nursing** (head-up positioning) keeps the pouch empty, and delayed primary **anastomosis** (surgical joining) follows radiologic **oesophageal elongation** (growth lengthening) usually at **4** (four) to **6** (six) months.

steps.say: Growth itself can be harnessed to close the gap. A stitch anchors the lower end to the backbone so every centimetre the baby grows stretches the food pipe longer. The older operation that cut the muscle and ruined swallowing is now abandoned.
steps.tx: The divided distal end can be hitched to **prevertebral fascia** (backbone sheet) with a **hemoclip** (metal marker) so growth provides **oesophageal lengthening** (stretch growth) for later joining. Abandoned **esophagomyotomy** (muscle-cut lengthening) is obsolete because it wrecks motility and causes lifelong **dysmotility** (swallowing failure), leaving a dead conduit.

steps.say: When the upper pouch cannot be managed safely, the neck is opened and the food pipe brought out to the skin. This last-resort opening controls drooling that threatens the lungs. Months later the staged plan replaces the missing segment with stomach, colon or small bowel.
steps.tx: **Cervical esophagostomy** (neck spit fistula) is reserved for unmanageable aspiration, and **oesophageal replacement** (substitute conduit) with stomach, colon or **small bowel** (jejunal graft) waits until **1** (one) to **2** (two) years of age. Between stages the gastrostomy sustains nutrition and growth.

steps.say: The gap is measured, not guessed. Dye pushed up through the stomach tube outlines the lower end while a metal-marked tube in the upper pouch shows the top. The distance on that paired picture decides between joining the native ends and borrowing colon. Repeat pictures track growth until the two ends meet without tension.
steps.tx: The **gap assessment** (length measurement) is judged by **contrast study** (dye swallow) through the **gastrostomy** (stomach tube) against an indwelling radiopaque upper tube, choosing primary joining versus **colonic interposition** (colon bridge). Accurate gap measurement avoids a doomed tight **anastomosis** (surgical join) under tension. Repeat imaging tracks growth until the ends meet without **tension** (stretch).

steps.say: A different child presents late with coughing on every feed but a normal swallow picture at first glance. The hidden channel sits high in the neck where windpipe meets food pipe, causing choking. Rigid scoping with a wire through the opening maps it for a small neck incision.
steps.tx: Isolated **H type fistula** (high neck channel) presents late with feeding cough and choking, is fixed through a **cervical incision** (neck cut) near the **thoracic inlet** (chest entrance), and is mapped by rigid **bronchoscopy** (windpipe scoping) with **guidewire cannulation** (wire marking). A **recurrent fistula** (reopened channel) is mapped the same way with **Fogarty catheter** (balloon marker) placement to guide **redo surgery** (repeat operation).

vis.alt: Side view diagram of a newborn chest and neck showing a blind upper food pipe pouch and a lower channel joining the windpipe.
vis.caption: Blind upper pouch with distal channel joining the windpipe. Credit: Jmarchn.

steps.say: The diagram shows the full defect family in one view, teaching classification. Five channel patterns run from isolated gaps to combined fistulas, the coiled tube on the chest film marks the blind pouch, and the associated spinal and limb defects remind you to screen the whole baby. Learn this picture and you can classify any case.
steps.tx: **Gross types** (five atresia patterns) with **X-ray** (chest film) and **VACTERL features** (spine, anus, heart, kidney, limb defects) classify every case: pure gap, proximal fistula, distal fistula, double fistula and isolated H channel. The coiled **nasogastric tube** (feeding tube) on film marks the blind upper pouch.

vis.alt: Five atresia fistula types with coiled feeding tube X-ray and antenatal and VACTERL features.
vis.caption: Five fistula patterns with coiled tube film and VACTERL associations. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Mortality follows the company the defect keeps, not the gap itself. A strong heart and normal chromosomes predict a straightforward course, while major cardiac or genetic disease dominates the risk. Full anomaly screening therefore precedes every repair plan.
steps.tx: **Mortality** (death risk) tracks **cardiac anomaly** (heart defect) and **chromosomal aberration** (genetic defect) rather than the atresia itself, so full anomaly screening sets **prognosis** (expected outcome) and precedes any repair plan. **Echocardiography** (heart scan) and **renal ultrasound** (kidney scan) with limb and spine review complete the VACTERL hunt.

steps.say: A right-sided body artery changes the whole operation, complicating repair. Arch anomalies cluster with these defects and raise the complication rate, and the side of the chest opening follows the arch. A plain film plus heart scan maps the arch before the incision is drawn.
steps.tx: A right sided **aortic arch** (right-looping body artery) raises arch anomalies and postoperative complications, influences **thoracotomy** (chest opening) side choice, and is defined by preoperative chest film and **echocardiography** (heart ultrasound). Either side suits a right arch; a left arch favours the right chest.
